newsitem.title: USA: U.S. said to target Sudan with aid to neighbors.
newsitem.headline: U.S. said to target Sudan with aid to neighbors.

text.p: The U.S. government will send nearly $20 million in surplus military equipment to Ethiopia, Uganda and Eritrea, which are collaborating to help overthrow the Islamic regime in Sudan, the Washington Post reported in its Sunday editions.

Assistant Secretary of State George Moose said the aid was intended for the governments of Ethiopia, Eritrea and Uganda in their own defence, adding, "Nothing we are giving them is to be used for any other purpose," the Post reported.
But it quoted congressional sources expressing scepticism that the aid would be kept from rebel forces fighting Sudan's militant regime.
Clinton administration and congressional officials told the paper all of the military aid was non-lethal and defensive, and included radios, uniforms, boosts and tents.
But congressional and Defence Department sources said the aid could be expanded to include rifles and other weapons.

The decision to provide military aid to the three African nations reflected growing administration anger at Sudan, which the White House considers second only to Iran as a staging ground for international terrorism.
